s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Skin lesions are present on periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Skin lesions are present on periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles

raw.rationale: The patient's 7-year medical history of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques, along with the presence of central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, are consistent with Erdheim-Chester Disease. The skin biopsy findings of a dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis with negative CD1a and S-100 and positive CD68 immunohistochemical results also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Negative CD1a and S-100 immunohistochemical results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Rosal-Dorfman Disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with lymphadenopathy and does not usually have the systemic involvement seen in this patient

rejected.label: Hand-Schuller-Christian Disease
rejected.why: A form of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis, which is not supported by the immunohistochemical results

rejected.label: Histiocytosis X
rejected.why: An outdated term that encompasses Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis, which is not supported by the immunohistochemical results
